anchorFacts: Five starters and one Carmen Mesa. Who is the odd arm out?

Pablo Almanzar took the rotation spot most expected Carmen Mesa to fill, then threw a no-hitter in his debut and a 1-hitter to close the ALCS. That leaves the rotation full with Coles, Ramos, Rivas, Ellis and Almanzar. Mesa sits at AAA on a $780K deal with nowhere to start in Oakland. Henry Rivas is the most expensive arm at $28. 2M and missed time this season before his complete game in World Series game 4.
Is Mesa the A's best trade chip this winter, and how long does the front office keep paying top dollar for Rivas while the cheap arms win?

angleRead.name: Tanya Cruz
angleRead.text: I'm standing at the back of the clubhouse where the light stays low and the offseason lockers are already half-emptied. The rotation board still has five names on it — Coles, Ramos, Rivas, Ellis, Almanzar — and somewhere down in AAA there's Carmen Mesa with a $780K deal and no door in. That's the thing that doesn't line up for me. Almanzar didn't just take the spot; he threw a no-hitter in his debut and a 1-hitter to close the ALCS. You don't send that back down. So the question isn't really who the odd arm out is — it's whether the front office has the stomach to admit it. Rivas is the most expensive arm at $28.2M and he missed time this season before his complete game in World Series game
